pulse.text: **Nothing shipped overnight** — no new models and no ranking change: Claude Opus 5 still holds sole #1 at **61** on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1, ahead of Claude Fable 5 (60) and GPT-5.6 Sol (59), and Polymarket's best-model-in-July market has hardened to **99.4% Anthropic** on $7.9M of volume. The market drift was small and one-directional: Google's next Gemini Pro ticked up to **85% by Aug 31** (Aug 7 still 22%, Jul 31 down to 3%), the Arena ceiling nudged to 89% for a 1500+ top Elo by Dec 31, and GPT-6 held flat at 89% by Dec 31 with Manifold unchanged at 60% before October. The news cycle has rotated off the OpenAI sandbox escape itself and onto the open-weight fight it started — **Nvidia, Microsoft and Meta warned against "premature restrictions"** on open weights the same week APEC's 21 economies issued a Chengdu statement backing open-source development, and CNBC reported the model that actually repelled the attack on Hugging Face was Z.ai's open-weight **GLM-5.2**. Compute kept compounding underneath all of it: AMD will put up to $5B into Anthropic for a 2-gigawatt MI450 deployment, and Alphabet lifted 2026 capex guidance to $190–205B. Two clocks to watch next: Moonshot's full **Kimi K3 open weights, still promised for Jul 27**, and the IMO gold market at **77%** with the Shanghai contest results pending.
